subject: Phase 100090: Shared Continuous EMA Update Engine
verdict_justification: The Phase 100090 implementation successfully delivers the shared continuous EMA and trend engine, durable definition-time update_rule declarations with epistemic_kind column separation, dual-backend persistence (SQLite and Postgres) with serializable concurrency, and the generic update rule splitter. All workspace test suites and the >=90% per-file line/function coverage gate pass cleanly. Five non-blocking findings were identified: an addressability mismatch in the update facade, header boundary compliance, discarded discrete new_value, empty-window recovery bypass, and unparameterized SQL LIMIT in SQLite.

issues.title: Inconsistent addressability between continuous and discrete update paths in update facade
issues.why_it_matters: The generic update(item_id, new_value, update_rule) entrypoint specified in §4.9.4.A takes target as item_id, but the implementation bifurcates target semantics: for continuous updates, target must be an attr_key; for discrete updates, target must be an item_id. Calling update with an attribute key for discrete updates returns ErrorCode::InvalidArgument ('discrete updates are item-addressed'), while calling update with an item_id for continuous updates fails with WrongUpdateRule.
issues.impact: Callers cannot use a uniform identifier scheme across update rules, and discrete updates on items cannot verify whether the item belongs to a continuous or discrete attribute schema.
issues.proposed_fix: Standardize target addressability across both paths; either allow discrete updates to accept attribute keys and look up current open items, or enable items to reference their declared attr_key so caller update_rule can be validated against item attribute schema.

issues.title: Missing boundary focus statement in newly added module headers
issues.why_it_matters: AGENTS.md defines a strict module header template requiring '//! Keep this module focused on <responsibility>.' under the '## Boundary' section. All newly created production modules in clio-types, clio-store, and clio-write omit this closing sentence.
issues.impact: Minor style and governance compliance defect against the repository's AGENTS.md rules.
issues.proposed_fix: Add the mandatory '//! Keep this module focused on <responsibility>.' closing line under ## Boundary in all newly created Rust source files.

issues.title: Discrete update routing silently discards new_value
issues.why_it_matters: The update facade takes new_value as an argument. In the continuous path, new_value is parsed into float and smoothed via EMA. In the discrete path, new_value is completely ignored and None is passed as replacement_id to invalidate(). While closing the prior item satisfies invalidation without bypassing Phase 100040 admission gates, discarding new_value silently without error or replacement linkage is unexpected.
issues.impact: Callers passing a new value expecting it to replace the discrete fact will only invalidate the existing fact without creating or linking a replacement.
issues.proposed_fix: Document why new_value cannot be admitted directly on the discrete branch without bypassing Phase 100040 admission gates, or accept an optional replacement ID for gated replacement.

issues.title: parse_window treats empty array '[]' as valid rather than falling back to series reconstruction
issues.why_it_matters: In parse_window, '[]' parses successfully as Some(vec![]). If continuous_state.window_json is corrupted with '[]' while continuous_observations has retained history points, observe_continuous_impl uses an empty prior window instead of triggering rebuild_window_from_points, resetting the EMA to cold start.
issues.impact: A corrupted empty window array causes unnecessary cold-start reset despite available historical observations.
issues.proposed_fix: Update parse_window to return None when the parsed array has zero elements (if window.is_empty() { return None; }), ensuring an empty window row triggers history rebuild from continuous_observations.

issues.title: Unparameterized LIMIT string formatting in sqlite_attribute.rs
issues.why_it_matters: continuous_series_impl in sqlite_attribute.rs formats capped as i64 directly into the SQL string via format!(... LIMIT {}, capped as i64) rather than binding it as a positional parameter LIMIT ?4.
issues.impact: Minor inconsistency with postgres_attribute.rs (which binds $4) and SQL formatting best practices.
issues.proposed_fix: Parameterize the LIMIT clause as LIMIT ?4 with params![bank_id, attr_key, as_of, capped as i64], matching postgres_attribute.rs.

dismissed: Non-encrypted numeric states in continuous_state/continuous_observations: Reviewed against §7.4 and Phase 100090 scope. DEK encryption applies to content-bearing payloads in items, whereas continuous scalar state is structured metadata; compliance erase of continuous series is explicitly scoped to slice 100190.

Postgres hashtext 32-bit advisory lock: Checked for collision impact. A 32-bit advisory lock hash collision only introduces brief lock serialization between different keys; data integrity is maintained by transactional WHERE bank_id AND attr_key clauses.
